thread:
arjun: thinking out loud — our cost dashboard ingest is exploding in volume. we currently sample uniformly which misses high-cost SKUs (long seqs + large models). proposal: SKU-aware sampling that biases towards high-token-cost requests while keeping overall ingest bounded.

kate: +1, we've been losing signal for the long-tail expensive queries. important for accurate per-model/unit econ. how would you weight SKUs?

arjun: simplest is weight by estimated token_cost = tokens * model_unit_cost, then do reservoir sampling with per-SKU weight threshold. e.g. keep 100% of requests where token_cost > $0.10, sample 10% where token_cost in [$0.01, $0.10], 1% below that.

peter: can we do this without adding latency on the request path? we can't call pricelist lookups synchronously.

arjun: yes — precompute model_unit_cost in the routing/edge layer (it's a tiny lookup) and attach a cost_tag to the request metadata. sampling decision in the telemetry sidecar will be O(1).

sara: for rollouts/canaries we also need deterministic sampling so we can compare canary vs prod. maybe seed sampling with request ID + route id so it's sticky?

arjun: agreed. plan: two-pass sampling logic: 1) deterministic sticky sample for experiment groups (hash(route + user_id) % 100 == x), 2) weighted reservoir sampling based on token_cost for everything else. sticky wins.

mo: what about chains (multi-model orchestration) — a single user request can fan out to many model calls. we should avoid double-counting when showing per-invocation cost.

arjun: good catch — the telemetry sidecar will emit a single root_event with aggregated tokens/cost when available. for fan-out we tag child calls as "child_of:<root_id>" and they are suppressed from per-invocation ingest unless explicitly sampled.

ellen: ops-bot FYI — this will change Kafka topic message rates to telemetry-raw by ~25% on heavy tenants. can we get a quick quota bump request? :eyes:

ops-bot: @eng-platform note: opened infra ticket INF-7892 for temporary ingestion quota increase. ETA 48h.

peter: small nit — the dashboard needs to surface sampling rate per route and per SKU so product understands confidence intervals. plus a flag to view only unsampled (raw) data when available.

arjun: yep — UI should show effective_sample_rate and estimated_bias. proposal for metadata in the record: {"sample_rate":"0.01","sampling_reason":"low_cost","weight_factor":"10x"}.

kate: can you sketch the sampling config? will it live in feature flags or config service?

arjun: config example (keeps it short):
```json
{
  "sampling_windows": [
    {"min_cost": 0.1, "sample_pct": 100},
    {"min_cost": 0.01, "sample_pct": 10},
    {"min_cost": 0.0, "sample_pct": 1}
  ],
  "sticky_experiments": true,
  "max_ingest_rps": 20000
}
```

sara: love it. add an override for tenant opt-in so we can ask big customers to opt into full traces for billing reconciliation.

arjun: yeah add "tenant_overrides": {"tenant_id": {"sample_pct": 100}} in the config.

mo: testing plan? want to avoid regressing billing dashboard accuracy.

arjun: rollout plan: feature-flag behind dev flag -> backend-only sampling dry-run (emit sample decision but still send all events) for 48h -> enable actual sampling for 5% of traffic -> monitor delta in per-SKU cost estimates vs baseline, aim for <2% deviation on aggregate top-50 SKUs -> ramp.

peter: add alert if top-50 SKUs estimate diverges >3% for 2 consecutive hours.

arjun: will add. action items: (1) arjun to make sampling prototype PR for telemetry sidecar, (2) kate to wire sample metadata into dashboard schema, (3) mo to mock fan-out suppression logic, (4) sara to draft tenant opt-in docs, (5) ops-bot to track INF-7892.

sara: thanks — I'll collect owners and set a 2-week cadence for the rollout. :+1:
